extracted.intended_audience: NLP/AI researchers and creative-writing educators evaluating LLM-generated fiction (researchers comparing LLMs and humans using human evaluation)
extracted.subtask_description: Human-evaluation of LLM-generated short fiction (zero-shot story generation) using a 10-item creative-writing rubric adapted for a prompt-specific task (epic single-combat story in the style of John Kennedy Toole), comparing multiple LLMs and human writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall/holistic/cohesive readability of the story
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall/holistic/cohesive readability of the story (not just a compilation of elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Part of the holistic scale (Emerging 1-4, Competent 5-8, Sophisticated 9-10). Intended to assess the text as a coherent whole (flow, readability, whether the story reads as an integrated narrative rather than a stitched-together set of elements). Rubric emphasizes holistic judgment over mere sum of analytic parts and is drawn from established craft guidance (Davidow & Williams 2016; Carey et al. 2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of key narrative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of key narrative elements - vocabulary choice, imagery, setting, themes, dialogue, characterisation, point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Raters evaluate richness and appropriateness of vocabulary and imagery, the effectiveness and consistency of setting and theme, naturalness and function of dialogue, depth and plausibility of characterization, and control of point of view. Grounded in craft practices (le mot juste, Strunk & White, Orwell, Dillard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural elements and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural elements and presentation which reflects the control of structural elements such as spelling, grammar, punctuation, paragraphing, and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Focus on technical correctness and presentation that supports readable, professional prose. Judges penalize lapses in mechanics that hinder comprehension. The rubric aims to measure craft skills without encouraging formulaic rule-based writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall plot logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall plot logic: hook, conflict, initial crisis, rising and falling action, denouement/ resolution (Freitag’s pyramid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Evaluates narrative structure and logical progression of plot elements (presence and execution of hook, conflict, escalation, climax, resolution). Raters consider whether plot development is coherent and credible within the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity/innovation/originality/research
rubrics_metrics.description: Creativity/innovation/originality/ research—credibility, new knowledge, avoidance of cliché and derivative tropes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Measures novelty, imaginative risk-taking, avoidance of clichés and derivative tropes, and credible creative choices. This is the criterion where human writers in the study tended to outperform LLMs; it is central to assessing 'creative' quality rather than technical competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of the John Kennedy Toole style
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of the John Kennedy Toole style of writing using the indicators/ characteristics listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Task-specific criterion: raters assess presence and quality of stylistic elements associated with John Kennedy Toole as given in the study's indicators (see Appendix C for detailed characteristics). This item evaluates how well the writer captures the named author's voice and stylistic markers while avoiding mere imitation or pastiche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and habitation of the epic genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding and habitation of the epic genre of heroic/legendary adventure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Judges assess whether the story convincingly occupies the epic/heroic genre space (tone, scope, stakes, grandiosity appropriate to an 'epic' narration) and whether genre expectations are satisfied or creatively subverted in service of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and credibility of a single combat scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Description and credibility of a single combat scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Focus on vivid, believable depiction of a single-combat encounter (sensory detail, choreography, pacing, believability in the storyworld). For the prompt used, this criterion evaluates the central action element required by the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate inclusion of specified main characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate inclusion of two main characters Ignatius J. Reilly and a pterodactyl in action and description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Task-specific: judges check that the two required protagonists are present and represented in ways that fit the prompt (action, description, characterization). Accuracy here includes fidelity to the character cues provided and plausibility within the story context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a characteristically dark humorous tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a characteristically dark humorous tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored out of 10 points. Assesses presence and effectiveness of dark/comic tone appropriate to the prompt and to Toole’s comic fiction tradition. The study notes humor is highly subjective and among the hardest rubric items (lowest average across models); raters evaluate whether humor is present, consistent, and stylistically appropriate rather than gratuitous.
